<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
For unmodulated waveforms $\omega(t)=\omega_0=\text{const.}$ we obtain
\begin{align}
\hat{y}(\tau,\ensuremath{\hat{t}}) &=  \int_{-\infty}^\tau 
 {h}(\tau-\tau')\,\hat{x}(\tau',\ensuremath{\hat{t}}-\omega_0\,(\tau-\tau'))\,\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}}\tau' \nonumber\\
&= \int_0^{\infty} 
  {h}(\tau')\,\hat{x}(\tau-\tau',\ensuremath{\hat{t}}-\omega_0\,\tau')\,\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}}\tau'
 \label{eq.5b}
\end{align}
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The theorem follows immediately from inserting the characteristic
    curve $(\tau,\,\ensuremath{\hat{t}}) = (t,\,\omega_0\,t+\Theta)$ in \eqref{eq.5b}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
One can see from (\ref{eq.5b})
that the convolution is performed along the characteristic curve.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{theo.1}
 The DAE \eqref{eq.3} and PDE solutions \eqref{eq.4} coincide along the
 characteristic curves if the equalities
	\begin{align}
	 & h(t-\tau')\, \hat{x}(\tau',\,\omega(\tau')\,\tau'+\Theta) \nonumber\\
	 &\qquad = \int_\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}
	      \hat{h}(t-\tau',\,\omega(t)\,t+\Theta-t')\,\hat{x}(\tau',\,t')\,\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t'
	      \label{eq.theo.1}
	\end{align}
	likewise
	\begin{align}
	 & h(\tau')\,\hat{x}(t-\tau',\,\varphi(t-\tau')+\Theta) = \nonumber\\
	 &\qquad \int_\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}\,
	      \hat{h}(\tau',\,t')\,\hat{x}(t-\tau',\,\omega(t)\,t+\Theta-t')\,\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t'
	      \label{eq.theo.2}
	\end{align}
 hold.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
From the uni-variate convolution one obtains
\begin{align*}
    y_\Theta(t) &= \int_{-\infty}^t h(t-\tau')\,x_\Theta(\tau')\,\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} \tau'
    = \int_0^\infty h(\tau')\,x_\Theta(t-\tau')\,\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} \tau'
\end{align*}
and since the DAE and PDE solutions coincide along the characteristic curves
$
 x_\Theta(t) = \hat{x}(t,\,\omega(t)\,t+\Theta)
$,
it follows that
\begin{align*}
    y_\Theta(t) &= \int_{-\infty}^t h(t-\tau')\,
       \hat{x}(\tau',\,\omega(\tau')\,\tau'+\Theta)\,\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} \tau'\\
       &= \int_0^\infty h(\tau')\,\hat{x}(t-\tau',\,\varphi(t-\tau')+\Theta)\,\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} \tau'
\end{align*}
Since
\[
 y_\Theta(t) = \hat{y}(t,\,\omega(t)\,t+\Theta)
\]
must hold along the characteristic curve for the output signal too, 
we obtain from the bi-variate convolution
\begin{align*}
    y_\Theta(t) &= \int_{-\infty}^t \int_\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}
      \hat{h}(t-\tau',\,\omega(t)\,t+
      \Theta-t')\,\hat{x}(\tau',\,t')\,\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t'\,\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} \tau'\\
      &= \int_0^\infty \int_\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}\,
      \hat{h}(\tau',\,t')\,\hat{x}(t-\tau',\,\omega(t)\,t+\Theta-t')\,\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t'\,\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} \tau'
\end{align*}
From comparison one concludes that
\begin{subequations}\label{eq.4a}
\begin{align}
 &  h(t-\tau')\, \hat{x}(\tau',\omega(\tau')\,\tau'+\Theta) = \nonumber \\
 &\qquad  \int_\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}
      \hat{h}(t-\tau',\omega(t)\,t+\Theta-t')\,\hat{x}(\tau',t')\,\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t' \\
 & \text{or equivalently} \nonumber \\
 & h(\tau')\,\hat{x}(t-\tau',\,\varphi(t-\tau')+\Theta) = \nonumber \\
 &\qquad  \int_\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}\,
      \hat{h}(\tau',\,t')\,\hat{x}(t-\tau',\,\omega(t)\,t+\Theta-t')\,\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t'
\end{align}
\end{subequations}
holds.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{theo.2}
    The equalities \eqref{eq.4a} of Theorem~\ref{theo.1} are fulfilled if
	\begin{equation}
	 \hat{h}(\tau,\,\hat{t}) = h(\tau)\,\delta(\hat{t} - \omega_0\,\tau) \label{70}
	\end{equation}
	where $\delta$ is the periodic Dirac distribution.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
From the sift property of Dirac's $\delta$ 
    distribution\footnote{Sift property: $\delta_T * x = x_T$.} it follows immediately
\begin{align*}
     &\int_\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}\,
      \hat{h}(\tau',\,t')\,\hat{x}(t-\tau',\,\omega_0\,t+\Theta-t')\,\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t'\\
	 & \qquad = \int_\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}} 
	 \delta(t'-\omega_0\,\tau')\,h(\tau')\,
	 \hat{x}(t-\tau',\,\omega_0\,t+\Theta-t')\,\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t'\\
	 &\qquad =  h(\tau')\,\hat{x}(t-\tau',\,\omega_0\,(t-\tau')+\Theta)
\end{align*}
Likewise
\begin{align*}
    &\int_\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}
      \hat{h}(t-\tau',\omega_0\,t+\Theta-t')\,\hat{x}(\tau',t')\,\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t'  \\
    &\qquad  = \int_\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}} \delta(\omega_0\,\tau'+\Theta-t')\, h(t-\tau')\,
    \hat{x}(\tau',t')\,\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t'  \\
    &\qquad = h(t-\tau')\, \hat{x}(\tau',\omega_0\,\tau'+\Theta)
\end{align*}
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{theo.3}
    Let $\omega(\tau)=\omega_0=\text{const.}$
    The equalities \eqref{eq.theo.1} and \eqref{eq.theo.2}
    are fulfilled if
	\begin{equation}
	 \hat{h}(\tau,\,\hat{t}) = h(\tau)\,\delta(\hat{t} - \omega_0\,\tau) =
	 \sum_k \frac{1}{2 \pi} h(\tau)\, \mathrm{e}^{-\jmath \, k\, \omega_0 \,\tau}
	 \,\mathrm{e}^{\jmath \,k\, \ensuremath{\hat{t}}} \label{80}
	\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
From the expansion \eqref{eq.6} and the orthogonality of the exponential function
 $<\mathrm{e}^{\jmath \,k\, t},\,\mathrm{e}^{\jmath \,l\, t}> \, = 2\,\pi\,\delta_{kl}$,
 where $< \cdot, \cdot >$ inner product and $\delta_{kl}$ is the Kronecker $\delta$ symbol,
 one obtains from \eqref{eq.5} immediately the integral \eqref{8a}.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
In RF circuit design the transfer function often shows bandpass behavior,
    i.e.\ the spectrum is concentrated around $k=\pm 1$ and with \eqref{8a}
    \[
        \hat{y}(\tau,\ensuremath{\hat{t}}) \approx \int_0^\infty h(\tau')\, 
        \mathrm{e}^{-\jmath \,( \omega_0 \,\tau' - \ensuremath{\hat{t}})}\,\hat{x}_1(\tau-\tau') +
     \mathrm{e}^{\jmath \,( \omega_0 \,\tau' - \ensuremath{\hat{t}})}\,\hat{x}_{-1}(\tau-\tau')\,\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} \tau'
    \]
    Since the modulated impulse response 
    $h(t)\,\mathrm{e}^{\mp\jmath \, \omega_0 \,t}
    \leftrightarrow H(\omega\pm \omega_0)$ exhibits lowpass, i.e.\ smooth, behavior, 
    the convolution integral \eqref{eq.8} can be calculated efficiently by a coarse
    discretization by, e.g., multistep integration methods.
    The equation \eqref{eq.8} shows similarity to the method of the equivalent 
    baseband  \cite{proakis2001digital} which is used in communication engineering
    for treating bandpass modulated signals efficiently, as considered in the next
    Section.
    However, the calculation of the analytical signal via the Hilbert transformation
    is not required.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{theo.4.2}
   Let $\omega(\tau)=\omega_0=\text{const.}$  The equality
 	\begin{equation}
	 \hat{h}(\tau,\,\hat{t}) = 
	 \sum_k \frac{1}{2 \pi} h(\tau)\, \mathrm{e}^{-\jmath \,  k\, \omega_0 \,\tau}
	 \,\mathrm{e}^{\jmath \,k\, \ensuremath{\hat{t}}} = h(\tau)\, \delta(\omega_0\,\tau - \ensuremath{\hat{t}}) \nonumber
              
	\end{equation}
holds.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Since
 \[
   \delta(t) = \frac{1}{T}\sum_k \mathrm{e}^{-\jmath \, 2\pi \, k\, t/T}
 \]
 holds on $\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}$, one gets from \eqref{80} the identity
 \begin{align}
 \hat{h}(\tau,\,\hat{t}) &= 
	 \frac{1}{2 \pi} h(\tau)\sum_k  \mathrm{e}^{-\jmath \, k \,\omega_0 \, \tau}
	 \,\mathrm{e}^{\jmath \,k\, \ensuremath{\hat{t}}} = \frac{1}{\omega_0} h(\tau)\,
	 \delta\left(\tau - \frac{\ensuremath{\hat{t}}}{\omega_0} \right)	 \nonumber\\
	 &= h(\tau)\sum_k \delta(\omega_0\,\tau - \ensuremath{\hat{t}})	 \nonumber
 \end{align}
 where the latter equality results from the identity $\delta(a\,t - t_0) = \frac{1}{\ensuremath{\left\lvert{a} \right\rvert}} 
 \delta\left(t - \frac{t_0}{a}\right)$.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
The ECB method as derived here ensures that the envelope and the RF signals
    have equal power. The scaling differs in literature.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
The transformation of LTI systems is equivalent to signals besides
    a multiplicative constant which ensures that the output envelope and
    RF signals have equal powers.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
The ECB signal $y_{BB}$ of $y_{RF} = h_{RF} * x_{RF}$ is given by
    $y_{BB} = h_{BB} * x_{BB}$, where $x_{BB}$ and $h_{BB}$ are the equivalent baseband signals
    of $x_{RF}$ and $h_{RF}$ given above.
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
The proof can be found in \cite{proakis2001digital}.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
